headline: MinerU’s MCP-enabled document pipeline can amplify prompt injection and cascading errors; other risks are mostly bounded by offline/local-only Great Expectations.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU exposes an MCP Server and processes rich document inputs; Great Expectations consumes validation results and documentation. If MinerU output is routed into Great Expectations without sanitization, document text can be treated as instructions or trusted content. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default integrations, though not proven from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF MinerU output is passed into Great Expectations as trusted text or config
IF an MCP bridge forwards document content without provenance labels
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of MinerU text into Great Expectations configs
Add a manual review step before any generated text is used as instructions
Strip executable directives from extracted documents
Use separate workspaces for raw documents and validation assets
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between MinerU and downstream consumers

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations is offline/network-egress none, while MinerU is allowlisted egress and reads local documents. The pair can still leak data if the same sensitive files are fed to MinerU and then exported through its API, but the blast radius is limited by Great Expectations’ lack of egress and the absence of shared filesystem write access.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are processed by MinerU and its API responses are shared externally
IF both agents are pointed at the same confidential source files
mitigations: Restrict MinerU to non-sensitive sample documents
Keep Great Expectations outputs in a separate local-only workspace
Review allowlisted egress destinations for MinerU
Redact sensitive fields before document extraction
requires-engineering: enforce data-class routing policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations can install packages and write validation artifacts, while MinerU cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or execute shells. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is read-only document handling plus MinerU’s API/MCP surface. No shared mutable resource is documented, so conflict risk stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory via an external orchestrator
IF an MCP tool exposes shared mutable state not listed in the profile
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Avoid concurrent writes to the same repo or workspace
Run MinerU and Great Expectations in separate sessions
Lock shared folders during validation runs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, and OCR that Great Expectations may use for validation or documentation. If Great Expectations treats MinerU output as authoritative without verification, extraction mistakes can cascade into incorrect tests or reports. The pathway is plausible from the profiles, but there is no direct evidence of automated action-taking, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Great Expectations consumes MinerU extraction output without human verification
IF validation rules are generated from OCR or table extraction results
mitigations: Require human review of extracted tables before validation
Compare MinerU output against source documents for critical fields
Flag low-confidence OCR for manual checking
Keep generated validation rules under version control review
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rejection logic

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation, while MinerU processes PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, images, and OCR text. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, so compliance risk is limited to generic handling of document data rather than a specific policy breach. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data flow.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through MinerU and then retained in Great Expectations outputs
IF local retention policies differ between the two tools
mitigations: Classify documents before processing
Avoid regulated data in shared validation runs
Set explicit retention windows for outputs
Store documentation separately from source data
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
